title: Wringer judge request
description: `request.json` — exactly what `wring judge` would send, written BEFORE any socket opens and written in dry-run mode too. That ordering is the point: what leaves the machine is auditable before it leaves, and a dry run produces the same artifact as a live one so there is something to read before deciding to send. Scrubbed by the redactor, so a rubric or a bundle carrying a secret does not put it on the wire OR in this file. Part of `wringer.judge.v1`. There is deliberately NO schema for `response.json`: it is the endpoint's arbitrary JSON body, and a schema for it could only be permissive enough to mean nothing.

temperature.description: Always 0. A judge that is not deterministic is not a gate, and a rubric verdict that changes between identical runs is an opinion rather than evidence.

messages.description: Exactly two: the system framing, then the user payload built from the bundle and the rubric.
